title: Angie's Got a Tape: Tupac, 30 Years in the Rearview
yt_title: The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez: Netflix Nov 27, Keffe D and the Lost 1996 Interview

slides.label: The tape
slides.text: In 1996, a *20-year-old Angie Martinez* flew to L.A. to interview *Tupac*. About *three months later*, he was shot in Las Vegas.

slides.label: Why it stayed buried
slides.text: Pac was *angry* and naming names at the peak of the *East vs. West* war. Angie held the tape for *30 years* so nobody would die over a conversation.

slides.label: The drop
slides.text: *The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez*, a *four-part series*, hits *Netflix Friday, Nov. 27*, with *Charlamagne, Big Boy, RZA, Lil' Cease* and more.

slides.label: Exhibit A
slides.text: *Keffe D* was found *guilty* of first-degree murder on Aug. 31 and sentenced to *40 years to life*. His *own interviews and memoir* convicted him.

slides.label: Exhibit B
slides.text: At trial, a retired detective repeated Keffe D's claim that *Puffy paid* for the hit. It was *never proven*. Combs was never charged and *denies it*.

slides.label: Dear Mama
slides.text: His mother *Afeni* was a *Black Panther* who beat the state *representing herself*, a month before he was born. He was named for a *Peruvian freedom fighter*.

slides.label: Two kings
slides.text: *Big* was killed six months after Pac, and that case is *still unsolved*. Puff's *I'll Be Missing You* sat at *No. 1 for 11 weeks*.

slides.label: In the rearview
slides.text: 80s babies remember *kids crying at school* in Sept. 1996. Thirty years later: *Brenda's got a baby. Angie's got a tape.*

caption_linkedin:
Angie's Got a Tape: Tupac, 30 Years in the Rearview

In 1996, a 20-year-old radio host made an editorial call most veterans would struggle with. Angie Martinez recorded a Tupac interview at the height of the East vs. West war and decided not to air it, because the risk was bigger than the ratings.

Thirty years later, The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez premieres on Netflix on Friday, Nov. 27. Same tape, new context: a courtroom verdict, a sentence of 40 years to life, and a culture ready to listen.

The lesson for founders and creators: timing and context are part of the product. Holding something back can be the move that protects its value.
